analysis.source: ZeroHedge (Tyler Durden), citing Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, FT and Bloomberg
analysis.title: Amazon, Broadcom Pile Into Off-Balance Sheet SPVs As AI Circularity "Undeniably Increasing"
key_insights: Amazon is reportedly sounding out investors on moving about $8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into an SPV that would raise debt, buy the chips and lease them back to Amazon (FT). Amazon would offer outside investors up to 10% of the SPV equity and keep no stake itself.

The Amazon SPV is expected to get an investment-grade rating on the strength of Amazon's AA credit, which opens it to insurers and pension funds. The stated goal is a 'more asset-light' balance sheet.

Amazon expects about $220B of capex this year. It planned about $50B of bond sales in March (upsized from $37B), but by the $25B July deal demand for long-dated paper had weakened and investors wanted higher yields.

The collateral is Grace Blackwell chips, which Nvidia's Vera Rubin is about to supersede. Amazon's filings assume each chip generation lasts at least five years. Once a third party lends against the chips, the useful-life assumption becomes the bondholders' recovery value.

The author cites Kashyap Sriram's claim that Nvidia books revenue upfront while Amazon depreciates chips over about six years even though they become worthless in under 3 years, and compares this to Enron's SPV playbook.

AWS is raising EC2 Capacity Blocks prices for machine learning by about 15% effective October 7 (per Goldman's Rich Privorotsky). It is the fourth straight quarterly increase and for the first time since January includes older A100 instances.

Broadcom's bank syndicate is starting to raise $60B of AI chip financing for Anthropic and other companies (Bloomberg): a $42B Class A senior-secured tranche and an $18B Class B junior tranche, with Blackstone leading and committing $9B of its own funds.

This follows the June Project 'Big Sky' ($35B raised by Apollo and Blackstone for Anthropic to buy Broadcom-made chips, with Broadcom backing the senior notes). The August talk of 'up to $100B' has shrunk to $60B. The platform is meant to finance more than 20 gigawatts of compute.

Morgan Stanley's tally lists $29B of chip-lease residual value support at Broadcom and up to $125B of potential residual value support at Nvidia from its $500B 'compute financing platform'. The FT confirmed the $125B figure.

Goldman's Privorotsky called Amazon's SPV a 'pretty standard evolution of the financing stack' but said he likes the Broadcom lending less: 'circularity is undeniably increasing but not today's problem.' The author notes the banks, not Broadcom, lend the $42B, with Broadcom guaranteeing the senior paper.

Circular links: Amazon has committed up to $83B to Anthropic, Anthropic rents AWS compute and leases Broadcom chips via the backstopped vehicle, Blackstone is an Anthropic investor, and Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor the Anthropic IPO with up to $10B. Anthropic is reportedly racing to IPO before Thanksgiving.

Goldman FICC data: hyperscaler bond issuance is on track for $250B in 2026 ($230B done) versus under $20B in 2024. Goldman credit strategists raised their 2027 forecast to $420B from $400B and assume 35% of 2027 hyperscaler capex is debt-funded. The $420B excludes SPV data center financings.

Hyperscalers are only 40% of the $575B+ of global AI-related debt issued this year. Since June 46.4% of hyperscaler issuance has been in the 0-5 year bucket, up from 29.9% in the first half, and 20-year-plus paper has dropped sharply.

Goldman's rates strategy (Will Marshall) says rate-insensitive investment plans weigh on duration risk appetite and could cause long-end yields to overshoot fair value. The 10-year is above 5.2% and the IG index yields about 5.95%, near 3-year highs.

Hyperscaler curves have steepened another 8bp relative to the market since August. AI single-name CDS volumes are up 400% year on year, and the liquid universe has grown from 4 names to 10-12 (ORCL, AVGO, NVDA, META, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT).

The off-balance sheet commitments of hyperscalers plus Nvidia and Broadcom reached $3.1T in August (Morgan Stanley), up from $1.8T in June. The author expects the Q3 update to show another increase. Rating agencies treat lease liabilities as debt, while the equity market mostly does not.

Risk framing: sale-leasebacks and vendor-guaranteed chip SPVs turn an operating risk into a credit risk. Oracle's $300B Project Jupiter in New Mexico, financed with bonds, loans and Blue Owl equity, is described as effectively mothballed with its loans down sharply. Broadcom CDS hit a record 122bps in August.

market_movers.rationale: Reported plan to move about $8B of Nvidia GB chips into a leased-back SPV. The author frames it as Enron-style off-balance sheet engineering and flags the chip depreciation assumptions.
Backs senior notes of a $60B AI chip financing vehicle, with $29B of residual value support per Morgan Stanley. The author says Broadcom CDS, a record 122bps in August, is the credit signal to watch.
Up to $125B of potential residual value support from its $500B compute financing platform, and reported talks to anchor the Anthropic IPO with up to $10B.
Bonds trade through B2/B levels per the author, and the $300B Project Jupiter is described as effectively mothballed.
Leading the $18B Class B junior tranche with $9B of its own funds. Its Anthropic stake reportedly flatters its private equity fund returns.

sector_views.rationale: The author argues AI capex financing is moving off balance sheet into SPVs, increasing circularity and hidden credit risk.
Hyperscaler curves have steepened, AI CDS volumes are up 400% y/y, and IG yields are near 3-year highs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman rates strategy links heavy, rate-insensitive AI issuance to weaker duration risk appetite and the risk of long-end yields overshooting fair value.
Near 3-year highs, which raises the cost of on-balance sheet funding and pushes issuers toward SPVs.
Mostly AWS chips and data centers, which drives the funding need.
Compared with under $20B in 2024. Goldman's 2027 forecast is $420B.

risk_factors: Sale-leasebacks and vendor-guaranteed SPVs turn an operating risk into a credit risk if demand for Blackwell-era compute disappoints.
Chip useful-life assumptions (five years or more) may overstate recovery value for SPV bondholders, with Vera Rubin about to supersede Grace Blackwell.
Off-balance sheet commitments ($3.1T) are understated in equity valuation, while rating agencies treat leases as debt.
Long-end yield overshoot from heavy, rate-insensitive AI issuance.
Stalled SPV-financed projects, as with Oracle's Project Jupiter, whose loans have fallen.
Circular financing among Amazon, Anthropic, Broadcom, Blackstone and Nvidia, plus the Anthropic IPO.
vol_and_positioning: AI single-name CDS volumes are up 400% year on year, and the liquid universe has grown from 4 names to 10-12 (ORCL, AVGO, NVDA, META, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT).
Broadcom CDS traded at a record 122bps in August. The author expects it to show whether credit is still paying attention.
Hyperscaler credit curves have steepened another 8bp relative to the market since August.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Privorotsky calls it a standard evolution of the financing stack as capex gets enormous. It is not a problem while compute stays scarce and AWS can raise prices every quarter.
tension_points.bear_case: SPVs turn an operating risk into a credit risk. Bondholders hold depreciating chips leased by a company that chose not to own them, and the structures only need growth to stop accelerating to break.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Utilization of compute falling or demand for Blackwell-era compute disappointing. Broadcom CDS widening from its record 122bps would also signal credit stress.
